initial_spec.task: Classify SCN5A transmembrane pore variant p.Asp1458Asn under ClinGen Channelopathy guidelines.
initial_assumptions: Room temperature patch clamp suggests severe loss of peak INa current (Brugada mechanism)
Suspected pathogenic via loss of function
constraints: Physiological temperature 37C recording required for functional evidence

evidence_schedule.content: VCEP Specification: SCN5A patch clamp functional assay PS3 requires mammalian expression at 37C physiological bath; room temperature assays cannot be scored.
Two case reports of sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS) are linked to a single multigenerational family with confirmed Long QT Type 3, not Brugada syndrome.

CONTRADICTION: Re-testing at 37C reveals peak INa current is completely normal (contradicting loss-of-function Brugada mechanism), but persistent late sodium current (INa,L) is increased 4-fold, establishing pure gain-of-function Long QT3 mechanism (PS3_Strong).

Variant is located in the DIII-DIV linker activation gate (PM1 hotspot) and completely absent in gnomAD v4 controls (PM2). Multi-family segregation reaches LOD = 3.8 (PS4/PP1). Classification reaches Pathogenic.

ground_truth.provenance: Established pathogenic LQT3 channelopathy mutation confirmed by physiological temperature assay.
